questions.stem: A shape has been moved without changing its size or orientation. Which transformation is this?
questions.explanation: A translation moves a shape without changing its size, shape, or orientation. It simply slides the shape to a new position.

questions.stem: Which transformation produces an image that is NOT congruent to the original?
questions.explanation: Translations, reflections, and rotations all produce congruent images. Only an enlargement with scale factor not equal to 1 changes the size.

questions.stem: A student describes a transformation as: 'A rotation of $90°$.' What information is missing?

options.text: The centre of rotation and direction
The equation of the mirror line

questions.explanation: To fully describe a rotation, you need the angle, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise), and the centre of rotation.

questions.stem: Shape A is the same size as shape B, but the orientation is reversed (laterally inverted). The transformation is most likely:
questions.explanation: A reflection is the only single transformation that reverses the orientation (laterally inverts) while keeping the size the same.

questions.stem: Two shapes are similar but not congruent. Which transformation maps one to the other?
questions.explanation: Similar but not congruent means the shapes have the same proportions but different sizes. Only an enlargement changes the size of a shape.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT needed when describing a reflection?

options.text: The equation of the mirror line
All of the above are needed

questions.explanation: Direction (clockwise/anticlockwise) is used to describe rotations, not reflections. A reflection requires the type of transformation and the equation of the mirror line.

questions.stem: Shape $B$ is an enlargement of shape $A$ with scale factor $\frac{1}{2}$. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Shape $B$ is half the size of shape $A$ in each linear dimension
Shape $B$ is the same size as shape $A$
Shape $B$ has half the number of sides as shape $A$

questions.explanation: A scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ means each length in the image is half the corresponding length in the original. The shape itself is unchanged.
